title: Multi-currency ledger
issue: A customer in Germany says her statement shows far more euros than she was sent from the US. Operations also say the FX-fee figures in the new fee report don't reconcile with what customers received. The test suite is red.

bugs.summary: When only the reverse pair is quoted (B/A), hop() multiplies by the rate instead of dividing.
bugs.symptom: The failing test is the EUR statement in statement.test.js, which points at statements.js; statements.js is correct.
bugs.spec: README, Exchange rates: "if A/B is quoted, multiply by it; if only B/A is quoted, divide by it".

bugs.visibility: visible only after the first fix (masked)
bugs.summary: The FX fee is 0.5% of the amount sent (sender currency) instead of 0.5% of the converted amount (receiver currency).
bugs.symptom: After fixing fx.js the EUR statement is still a few cents off. A comment in fees.js argues for the wrong behaviour.
bugs.spec: README, Transfers: "Cross-currency transfers pay 0.5% of the converted amount (in the receiver's currency, rounded half-up to its minor unit)".

bugs.summary: A retry that arrives while the first attempt is still running is not recognised (the key is only recorded after the operation finishes), so the transfer happens twice.
bugs.symptom: The visible idempotency tests retry sequentially, which works.
bugs.spec: README, Transfers: "A retry returns the original result — also when the retry arrives while the first attempt is still being processed. A transfer that failed does not use up its key".

distractors: concurrency.test.js fires 20 transfers at once and looks flaky; the per-account locks make it deterministic
TODO in accounts.js about negative balances (overdrafts are allowed by design)
TODO in interest.js about leap years (Actual/365 Fixed is intended)
the lock manager in locks.js looks intricate but is correct
